topic: You are looking at the past
hook: The Sun you see is 8 minutes old.
claim: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth, so we see the Sun (and every star) as it was when the light left it.
why_now: Light-travel-time Short at 300x breakout, 1.8M views this month
visuals: NASA SDO Sun footage, Hubble deep field, ISS sunrise

topic: Why you can't nuke a hurricane
hook: A hurricane releases more energy than a nuke. Constantly.
claim: A mature hurricane's heat release is like a 10-megaton bomb going off every 20 minutes, so a nuclear blast would not stop it and would spread fallout (NOAA HRD FAQ).
why_now: 'What if we nuked a hurricane' Short at 23x and 1.3K VPH; rising keyword 'disasters explained' +232%; Typhoon Arnab in NASA EO
visuals: NASA ISS and GOES hurricane footage, eye-of-storm flyovers

hook: Space is full of sunlight. So why is it black?
claim: Our sky looks blue because air molecules scatter blue sunlight toward our eyes; in space there is almost no air to scatter light, so the sky looks black even in full sunlight.
why_now: 'Why is space pitch black?' Short at 41x this week; 'real color of space' cluster breaking out
visuals: NASA spacewalk footage against black sky, ISS view of Earth's blue limb

hook: The Sun isn't yellow. It's white.
claim: The Sun emits all visible colors, which combine to white; it looks yellow from the ground because the atmosphere scatters away some blue light.
why_now: TikTok on the Sun's real color: 1M views at 34.9x this month
visuals: ISS photos of the Sun from orbit, NASA SDO, sunset from ISS

hook: Auroras are the Sun hitting our air.
claim: Charged particles from the Sun, steered by Earth's magnetic field, collide with oxygen and nitrogen high in the atmosphere, which then glow green, red, and purple.
why_now: Solar Cycle 25 peak; G2 storm watch Oct 8-9 put aurora in reach of up to 22 US states
visuals: NASA ISS aurora time-lapses, SDO solar flare footage

hook: The Moon is leaving us. Slowly.
claim: The Moon moves about 3.8 cm farther from Earth each year because of tidal interactions.
why_now: 'What if' niche surging (ifverse +52,580%); 'what would happen if the moon crashed into earth?' +725%
visuals: NASA LRO Moon footage, Apollo laser retroreflector photos, Earthrise

hook: The Pacific is heating up. Your weather will feel it.
claim: El Niño is a periodic warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific surface, tied to weaker trade winds, that shifts weather patterns worldwide.
why_now: NASA says a possibly record El Niño is unfolding (NOAA odds cited ~75-83% for strongest since 1950); NASA satellite articles late Oct 2026
visuals: NASA Sentinel-6/SWOT sea-surface-height animations, NASA SVS El Nino visualizations (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5683), PACE chlorophyll maps

topic: Why we only see one side of the Moon
hook: You've never seen the other side of the Moon.
claim: The Moon rotates once per orbit (tidal locking), so the same face always points at Earth; the far side was imaged directly by crews on Artemis II.
why_now: NASA released 800+ GB of Artemis II lunar science data and 11,000+ images on Oct 7, 2026
visuals: NASA LRO far-side imagery, Artemis II flyby gallery (check each item credit), Earthrise

hook: Saturn is light enough to float on water.
claim: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm3, less than water at 1.0, because it is mostly hydrogen and helium (it would need an impossibly large ocean).
why_now: Saturn reached opposition Oct 4, 2026 (NASA skywatching guide); no direct viral link found, demand score is low
visuals: NASA Cassini Saturn imagery and rings, Hubble Saturn portraits

topic: Venus day is longer than its year
hook: On Venus, a day lasts longer than a year.
claim: Venus rotates once in about 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in about 225 Earth days.
why_now: Evergreen planet-fact format; Uranus facts TikTok at 15x and TOI-700 d Reel at 66x show planet-fact demand (see 2026-10-30 report)
visuals: NASA Magellan radar globes, Akatsuki/Mariner 10 Venus imagery, Venus animations

topic: Seasons are not caused by distance
hook: Summer isn't caused by being closer to the Sun.
claim: Earth's axis is tilted 23.4 degrees; the hemisphere leaning toward the Sun gets more direct sunlight and has summer. Distance is not the cause (verify perihelion/aphelion dates and distances on a NASA page before scripting).
why_now: Evergreen myth-bust; northern winter approaching, daylight-change questions peak (no direct metric found)
visuals: NASA SVS/EPIC Earth-from-space animations, DSCOVR EPIC imagery, NASA Earth tilt diagrams

topic: Why stars twinkle but planets don't
hook: Stars twinkle. Planets don't. Here's why.
claim: Stars are so far away they are point sources, so turbulent air bends their light around and they flicker; planets show a tiny disk whose many points average out.
why_now: IG Reel on this exact question: 843.5K views at 35.8x this month
visuals: NASA night-sky footage, ISS photos of atmosphere layer, planets (Jupiter, Venus) imagery

hook: Martian dirt could poison astronauts.
claim: Martian soil contains perchlorates and fine dust that would be hazardous for crews; NASA's Perseverance is gathering data to protect future explorers.
why_now: IG Reel 3.4M views; NASA Perseverance dust article published 3 days ago
visuals: Perseverance and Curiosity rover imagery, Mars dust storm footage

hook: One teaspoon of this weighs a billion tons.
claim: Neutron stars pack more than the Sun's mass into a city-sized ball, so a sugar-cube-sized piece would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
why_now: Pulsar-density Reel: 770K views at 144x this month
visuals: NASA Goddard SVS pulsar and neutron-star animations, Crab Nebula (Hubble/Chandra)

hook: Mars is red because it is rusty.
claim: NASA says Mars looks reddish due to oxidization: iron in its rocks, soil and dust rusts, and dust in the air makes the planet look red.
why_now: Follows Mars dust video; planet-fact demand from 2026-10-30 report (Uranus 15x, TOI-700 d 66x)
visuals: NASA Perseverance/Curiosity rover imagery, MRO HiRISE, Viking global mosaics

hook: Frozen ground holds more carbon than the sky.
claim: Permafrost soils hold roughly twice as much carbon as is currently in the atmosphere; thawing lets microbes release it as CO2 and methane.
why_now: Rising keyword 'permafrost' +915% (~931K est. monthly searches)
visuals: NASA ABoVE Arctic footage, Landsat thaw-lake imagery, Earth Observatory Arctic images

hook: Hurricanes always spin the same way. Here is why.
claim: Earth's rotation (the Coriolis effect) deflects air flowing toward a low-pressure center, so storms spin counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern.
why_now: Follows the hurricane series after the 'nuke a hurricane' breakout (23x); Hurricane Simon in NASA news feed
visuals: NASA ISS and GOES hurricane footage, NASA SVS global storm animations

hook: Shooting stars are mostly grains of dust.
claim: Most meteors are specks of comet or asteroid debris, many no bigger than a grain of sand, that glow as they hit the atmosphere at high speed; the Orionids come from Halley's Comet debris.
why_now: Orionid shower peaked Oct 21-22, 2026 (NASA skywatching); Leonids peak mid-Nov; demand evidence weak
visuals: NASA all-sky meteor camera clips, ISS meteor footage (check credits)

hook: These meteors hit at 43 miles per second.
claim: Leonid meteors move about 43.5 mi/s (69.7 km/s) and come from comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle (33-year orbit); meteor storms of 1,000+ per hour recur about every 33 years, last in 2002. 2026 peak Nov 16-17 but NASA expects under 3/hour. Partly overlaps shooting-stars video; angle is speed and the comet.
why_now: Leonids active Nov 6-30, peak Nov 16-17 (NASA); seasonal skywatching interest
visuals: NASA all-sky meteor camera clips, ISS meteor footage, Tempel-Tuttle illustrations (check credits)

topic: Great Red Spot is wider than Earth
hook: Jupiter has a storm twice as wide as Earth.
claim: The Great Red Spot is a swirling oval of clouds about twice as wide as Earth, and astronomers have tracked it for more than three centuries. Do not claim shrinkage without a NASA source.
why_now: Evergreen big-numbers format; no direct metric found
visuals: NASA Juno JunoCam and Voyager/Hubble Jupiter imagery (check credits; JunoCam citizen-processed items need care)

topic: Arctic winter ice ties record low
hook: The Arctic's winter ice just tied its record low.
claim: NASA and NSIDC report the March 2026 Arctic maximum, about 14.29 million sq km, matched the lowest winter maximum since satellite records began in 1979; the September minimum was only tenth lowest, so avoid implying a straight-line trend.
why_now: NASA/NSIDC 2026 sea ice releases; Antarctic ice near record low for date in Oct (NSIDC sources disagree, skip that claim)
visuals: NASA SVS Arctic sea ice animations (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5677), Earth Observatory maps

hook: Uranus spins on its side.
claim: Uranus is tilted about 98 degrees, so it rolls around the Sun like a ball, with 21-year polar day and night.
why_now: Uranus facts TikTok at 15x (1.6M views) in 2026-10-30 report; picked directly because queue was empty and research had already run today
visuals: NASA Voyager 2 images

topic: The Sun's atmosphere is hotter than its surface
hook: The Sun's air is hotter than its surface.
claim: NASA says the corona is much hotter than the photosphere (surface) and why is an open question Parker Solar Probe is studying. Get the temperature figures (about 1 million C vs about 5,500 C) from a NASA page before scripting; none were confirmed this run.
why_now: Parker Solar Probe 2026 close passes in NASA news; Solar Cycle 25 interest
visuals: NASA SDO corona footage, Parker Solar Probe WISPR imagery, eclipse corona images
